title: Aviation Ordnance Officer (II/III) (LtCol to Capt) and (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC AVN
raw_text:
1. MOS 6502, Aviation Ordnance Officer (II/III) (LtCol to Capt) and (CWO5 to
WO) PMOS, DC AVN

    a. Summary. The Aviation Ordnance Officer manages all aviation ordnance
logistics, maintenance, and operations functions, as well as all aircraft
weapon systems and Aircraft Armament Systems (AAS).

       b.    Prerequisites

             (1) LDOs must also achieve selection by the board to LDO.

        (2) Must have previously served in one of the following MOSs 6531,
6541, or 6591.

        (3) Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in
MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.

        (4) Security requirement: secret security clearance eligibility
(some key billets require top secret security clearance eligibility).

        (5) WOs/CWOs must have successfully completed the Aviation Ordnance
AO "A" Enlisted Course (N23G3U2) and must have demonstrated aviation ordnance
qualification and expertise through substantially documented performance of
associated duties and tasks.

       c.    Requirements

        (1) Warrant Officers must complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course
(WOBC) (M02RMN4) within 18 months of appointment to WO.

        (2) Warrant Officers must successfully complete the Aviation Ordnance
Managers Career Progression Level I (AOMCP) Course (N42G3N3), NAS Whiting
Field, FL.

        (3) CWO3s and LDO Captains should complete the Aviation Ordnance
Managers Career Progression Level II (AOMCP) Course (N42G4N3), NAS Whiting
Field, FL.

        (4) CWO4s, CWO5s, LDO majors, and LtCols should complete the Aviation
Ordnance Managers Career Progression Level III Course (N42G4M3), NAS Whiting
Field, FL.

        (5) Marines serving in billets coded with an additional skill
designator (ASD) as per the table of organization must attain the appropriate
skill within 24 months of billet assignment.

       d.    Duties

        (1) Direct and supervise all personnel engaged in the storage,
handling, transportation, inventory, maintenance, issue, and repair of
aviation munitions, AAS, and Armament Weapons Support Equipment (AWSE).

        (2) Manage the assignment and execution of all work task codes
authorized via the personnel qualification/certification program for Class V
ammunition and explosives.




                                         1-247                           Enclosure (1)
 1137                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



        (3) Evaluate aviation ordnance policies, processes and procedures for
accuracy, thoroughness, efficiency, and compliance with higher policy/
doctrine and promulgate changes when necessary.

        (4) Direct and supervise the aircraft armament system program,
ensuring all equipment adheres to associated documentation, repair and
provisioning processes and standards.

        (5) Direct the command explosives safety program and serve as the
command explosives safety officer.

        (6) Manage the command Class V(A) inventory accuracy and inventory
management programs.

        (7) Administer the explosive handler’s qualification and
certification program and serve as the certification board chairperson.

        (8) Promulgate and publish command aviation ordnance standard
operating procedures and ensure timely submission of all required aviation
ordnance reports.

        (9) Supervise the allocation, requisitioning, positioning, receipt,
status and the ammunition transaction reporting of the command's aviation
munitions.

        (10) Pursue defense acquisition workforce improvement (DAWIA)
certification in order to gain qualifications prior to entering senior
billets within the MOS (see MOS 8060). The two primary areas of study
typically applicable to AVLOG are:

               (a) Life cycle logistics (LCL).

               (b) Program management (PM).

    e.      Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
None.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

d. Duties (1) Direct and supervise all personnel engaged in the storage, handling, transportation, inventory, maintenance, issue, and repair of aviation munitions, AAS, and Armament Weapons Support Equipment (AWSE).
(2) Manage the assignment and execution of all work task codes authorized via the personnel qualification/certification program for Class V ammunition and explosives.
Recommend changes in rules, policies, standards, and regulations, based on knowledge of operating conditions, aircraft improvements, and other factors.
(3) Evaluate aviation ordnance policies, processes and procedures for accuracy, thoroughness, efficiency, and compliance with higher policy/ doctrine and promulgate changes when necessary.
Inspect work of aircraft mechanics performing maintenance, modification, or repair and overhaul of aircraft and aircraft mechanical systems to ensure adherence to standards and procedures.
(4) Direct and supervise the aircraft armament system program, ensuring all equipment adheres to associated documentation, repair and provisioning processes and standards.
Move and store inventories of explosives, loaded perforating guns, and other materials, according to established safety procedures.
(5) Direct the command explosives safety program and serve as the command explosives safety officer.
Classify and assign registration numbers to artifacts and supervise inventory control.
(6) Manage the command Class V(A) inventory accuracy and inventory management programs.
Establish, teach, and monitor students' compliance with safety rules for handling chemicals, equipment, and other hazardous materials.
(7) Administer the explosive handler’s qualification and certification program and serve as the certification board chairperson.
Review and edit standard operating procedures.
(8) Promulgate and publish command aviation ordnance standard operating procedures and ensure timely submission of all required aviation ordnance reports.
Plan, supervise, and review work of assigned subordinates.
(9) Supervise the allocation, requisitioning, positioning, receipt, status and the ammunition transaction reporting of the command's aviation munitions.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
